chunks: Because of the wickedness of some among the Jews, and because they obstructed people from the way of God, We forbade them many things which were lawful for them;
ai.seo_question: Why did God forbid the Jews things that were previously lawful for them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a specific divine punishment where the Jews were deprived of the 'good things' (tayyibat) previously permitted to them, such as certain foods and marital freedoms, due to their cumulative sins. The prohibition is linked not only to their general transgressions but specifically to their obstruction of the Israelites and others from following the path of God, highlighting a shift in their legal status as a consequence of spiritual deviation.
